common_assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert Borel space with canonical volume; rank zero is an explicit extension of the source Euclidean convention. V:E→ℝ is C²; 0<α≤β; α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for every x,v; η>0 and βη≤1. μ=volume.tilted(−V), J=Law(X,X+√ηZ) for independent X∼μ and Z∼N(0,I), and ν=J.snd. Finite dimensionality of E does not imply finite dimensionality of L²(ν).
source_attribution: ASTIS background completion and actual PBPS Appendix B/D consumer; faithful attributed restatement, not verbatim paper theorem.
route_boundary: The selected implementation route proves the squared-defect quadratic identity using selfadjoint contraction. The printed B5 joint P/U block identity has its independent source edges retained; it is not claimed proved by this scalar argument.

units.title: Actual centered selfadjoint operator and positive squared defect

steps.title: Recover the actual kernel and Hilbert operators
steps.text: Reuse the compiled actual Gaussian augmentation, reflected conditional kernel S, isometric reflection U, second-coordinate pullback M, and operator T. The kernel has the literal normalized density exp(−V((y+x)/2)−‖y−x‖²/(8η)); its stationary law and probability normalization are conclusions, not supplied premises.

steps.title: Transport selfadjointness
steps.text: The actual conditional expectation P is an orthogonal projection and U is selfadjoint. Move P across the inner product and use PM=M; the isometry M transfers the resulting symmetry to T.

steps.title: Prove mean preservation with the actual joint law
steps.text: The reflected joint law Λ disintegrates as ν⊗S and has second marginal ν. Each L² function is integrable because ν is a probability. The actual AE formula for T and Fubini therefore give mean preservation.

steps.title: Identify the constant and the entire centered space
steps.text: Take the canonical L² constant q=1. Its inner product is the mean. Selfadjointness and mean preservation imply Tq=q. The kernel of the continuous functional inner(q,·) is exactly all mean-zero classes, is closed, and is preserved by T.

steps.title: Restrict the actual operator
steps.text: Restrict T to the closed invariant subspace H₀. Its action as an ambient L² class is exactly T; symmetry and the norm bound transfer to this same restriction T₀.

steps.title: Compute both squared defects
steps.text: For either selfadjoint contraction, move one copy of T across the inner product. The result is nonnegative, so D=I−T² and D₀=I−T₀² are positive. Dq=0, and the centered defect is the actual restriction of D.

units.title: Exact centered squared-defect coercivity and bounded inverse

steps.title: Use the same actual reflection and actual pullback
steps.text: Compare the AE reflection actions to identify the operator U in the verified macroscopic contraction. For the actual M from the producer, PM=M gives macro-range membership. Its AE action Mu(x,y)=u(y) and the actual marginal ν=J.snd give mean transport directly, so centered u yields a centered macro input. No extra onto witness or copied Poincare proof is needed.

steps.title: Transport the exact sharp contraction
steps.text: Apply the verified sharp macro contraction to Mu. The actual identity MT=PUPM and the isometry transfer the constant without changing laws or operators.

steps.title: Derive the positive coercivity constant
steps.text: Square the contraction and use the actual quadratic defect identity. Since 0<αη≤1, the exact scalar identity yields a strictly positive lower bound, including the endpoint αη=1.

steps.title: Obtain a bounded inverse on the centered space
steps.text: The centered kernel is a complete Hilbert space because it is closed in L². Apply the fixed Mathlib coercivity-to-unit theorem to D₀ with δ. IsUnit means that an inverse exists in the algebra of bounded continuous linear endomorphisms of this same centered space. In the norm hypothesis, nonnegativity of the quadratic form follows directly from the already proved δ gap.

remaining: Positive square root Γ, its inverse/polar adapter, full weak H1 estimates, B13/B14, discrete hypocoercivity, event-process nonexplosion and invariance, mixing, implementation errors, query costs and actual-input composition remain open. IsUnit(D₀) does not prove any Γ result or full-space invertibility.
